# P35.16 — Geometry defects at ingest: axis order, detectors, correction claims, portal rows

**Ticket:** `docs/tickets/296_P35.16__geometry-defects-at-ingest.md` (manifest row **296** / catalog `R11-DATA-01`, Round 11 / P35, sub-round 11B; owned finding **F-322 (S1)**; `live_verification=false` invoked — the ticket's own `Run:` line is overridden). **Requirement ids stamped:** **F-322** (owned finding); cited context: **SIG-GEO-008** (geometry correctness at ingest — the axis order is a declared feed property), **SIG-IDENT-004** (never assert a location the evidence does not support — a defect-marked point publishes no device coordinate), **SIG-ONTO-011** (correction-by-new-claim), SIG-INGEST-033 (the closed predicate allowlist `geometry_defect` registers through), ADR-113 (`is_replay` evidence links), ADR-092 (observation-level row semantics the manifest disclosure rests on). **Base:** `r11/P35.13-provenance-stamp-release-json-headers` · **Live leg:** the hosted correction-claim writes are OM-20-listed (the GATE-G4 §4 list names this row verbatim) but this run's explicit `live_verification=false` keeps the pass **staged, not applied** — the committed `sig.geometry-corrections/1` artifact + dry-run report are the staged payload; the hosted leg re-runs under the ticket's own OM-19 re-run prompt.

## What ships

- **Declaration.** Every camera-registry + `dot_511` target row carries an explicit `axis_order` (`lon-lat`/`lat-lon`, closed vocabulary; `lat-lon` declared for `nottingham_gb_cctv_cameras` and `mark43_cctv` — the F-322 transposed-serve targets). A committed row without the field fails `sig-connectors validate`; the documented `lon-lat` default exists for synthetic/run-time targets only, never a silent registry guess. `jurisdiction_extents.toml` (new, 85 `(scheme, code)` rows) + optional per-target `extent` give every keyed target a resolvable detector bound; `sig.unresolved` rows record a skip, never a silent pass.
- **Detection.** `connectors/dot_511.py`: `detect_geometry_defect` runs on the publisher's raw interpreted pair **before** the parcel screen and tier transform — precedence `null_island` (within 1° of (0,0)) → `axis_swap` (outside the declared bound, transpose inside) → `sign_flip` (exactly one negated axis rescues) → `wrong_jurisdiction` (outside, unrescued). The verdict MARKS: the entity row carries `axis_order` + the `geometry_defect` evidence block, a `geometry_defect` claim emits (class + observed pair + declared bound + detector build `sig.p35-16-geometry-detector/1`), and **no** `camera_latitude`/`camera_longitude` claim asserts the defective pair; `camera_coordinate_source` still records which read produced it. Named field pairs stay name-authoritative under either order — a swapped named column flags, never silently relabels.
- **Vocabulary.** `geometry_defect` registered in `ontology/vocab/predicates.yaml` (string, multi-cardinality, immutable, `never_resolve`) + regenerated ontology artifacts + insert-only sqitch change `vocab_geometry_defect` (predicate row + 20-genre `directness_matrix` rows, `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`; revert refuses to drop a referenced row) + `dot_511_vocab.toml` allowlist entry (vocab `2026.10.17`).
- **Correction pass.** `db/src/db/geometry_corrections.py` + `sig-connectors geometry-corrections --dsn … [--apply] [--commit-chunk-size] [--code-commit]`: scope resolves from the committed `connectors/data/geometry_corrections.toml` (`sig.geometry-corrections/1` — the seven F-322 groups) through the *same* bound resolution the ingest detectors use; the dry-run plan is the apply plan — per subject it emits one `geometry_defect` marking claim citing the original coordinate claims via `derived_from_claim_ids`, and for provable `axis_swap` rows it mints transposed `camera_latitude`/`camera_longitude` correction claims carrying `revises_claim` + `correction_reason='axis_swap'`. Originals are read, never touched — all writes go through `PgClaimSink` (`is_replay`, chunked commits, content-digest idempotence), the closed-vocabulary precheck refuses before any write, and an out-of-scope flag scan counts flagged subjects on other keyed targets (disclosed, never written).
- **Portal row-count truth.** `exports/manifest.py` `Artifact` + `exports/bundle.py`: the manifest serializes `distinct_entities` beside `row_count` for entity-bearing tables (`None` where no `entity_id` column exists) — observation-level rows and licence-compartment splits are disclosed, never inflated into a census.
